BiblicalUsage: The name stands once in Scripture, joined to Laish, the father of Phaltiel, from whom Michal was taken and brought back to David. Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, and the single mention fixes the name in the middle of the struggle over David's house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even one mention is enough to show how costly the quarrels of kings were for ordinary people caught between them.
